title: Binance executives say approximately $6.34 billion in assets were affected by October 29 attack that began with fake job interviews
date_note: Date of the WuBlockchain article relaying the executives' statements; the page gives no earlier day for them. The attack itself is dated 29 October by Binance's incident report as relayed by BleepingComputer.
geo_basis: no place stated in the sources
summary: WuBlockchain relays Binance executives saying approximately $6.34 billion in crypto assets were affected and around $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted. Binance's chief security officer says an engineer was approached in September through a recruitment platform and given a coding assignment that contained malware. BleepingComputer reports that the FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor.
plain: Binance executives say approximately $6.34 billion in crypto assets were affected in the 29 October attack. They say it began with a fake job interview that gave an engineer a malicious coding assignment.
exec: Binance executives put the affected assets at approximately $6.34 billion and say around $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted.

evidence.quote: Approximately $6.34 billion in crypto assets were affected.
So far, around $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted.

validation.note: Two independent publishers, WuBlockchain and BleepingComputer, each report Binance's own account of the 29 October attack; Binance's own incident report was not read directly. WuBlockchain says the figures and recovery claims rest on Binance's statements and are not independently verified.

review.note: figure qualifier: title and plain said 'about' for $6.34 billion, source says 'Approximately'; rest checked against WuBlockchain and BleepingComputer
